title: Request-context evolution: SDK adapter for non-linear request flows
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Problem: Our current SDK propagation model assumes a mostly-linear request lifecycle (HTTP request -> one synchronous call path). Real production flows at Redwood include non-linear patterns: async callbacks, background jobs, queue replays, websocket multiplexing, and retry forks. We see gaps in trace continuity, high cardinality baggage growth, and edge-case attribution errors when requests are resumed across threads/processes.

Goal: Build a lightweight, opt-in SDK adapter and middleware hooks that: 1) preserve causal relationships across non-linear transitions (pause/resume, fork/join, handoff to worker), 2) bound baggage growth and enforce sampling coherence, 3) are low-overhead for hot paths, and 4) remain compatible with existing request carriers and Redwood tracing backend.

Scope and deliverables:
- SDK adapter: explicit save/restore and attach APIs for languages we own (Node, Python, Go), with deterministic semantics for parent/child attribution.
- Middleware hooks: web and worker integrations that call the adapter APIs on durable handoffs (queue put/get, websocket connect, cron job start).
- Context evolution policy: rules for merging baggage on forks, TTL for key-value entries, and a small canonical set of attributes preserved automatically (request-id, customer-id-hash, routing-tag).
- Sampling reconcile: strategy for reconciling sampling decisions when spans are resumed in a different process (prefer upstream sampling decision, with bounded override path).
- Backwards compatibility: graceful no-op behavior for older SDKs; a compatibility header that carries minimal rehydration metadata.

Success criteria / acceptance tests:
- End-to-end trace continuity for a sample app that forks to background workers: 95% of traces maintain a single root and correct parent-child edges.
- P50 overhead of adapter calls < 150ns in hot path benchmarks; P99 < 1ms.
- Baggage size per trace limited to 128 bytes by default; ability to opt-up with explicit API.
- Integration tests added for websocket resume, queued retry, and cron-driven replays.

Migration and rollout:
- Feature gated behind SDK opt-in flag and runtime config.
- Canary rollout in dev and staging, then internal Redwood services, then public SDK release.
- Observability: new dashboards to track "context rehydration failures", "baggage growth alerts", and "sampling-mismatch rate".

Open questions:
- Should we include cryptographic signing of rehydration blobs to prevent tampering in cross-tenant queues? (security team req?)
- How to handle third-party queues (SQS/Kafka) where size limits and encoding restrictions apply?

Notes: design doc and diagrams: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Request+Context+Evolution
Proof-of-concept repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ctx-evolution-poc
comments: 2025-02-21 — Kickoff: scoped work with PM (Jared Wells) and DRI (Trace infra). Decided to prototype Node adapter first because it's used by most gateway services.

2025-02-25 — Spike complete: PoC shows save/rehydrate API adds ~120ns on x86 for a minimal keyset. Memory allocs are the primary cost; exploring object pool for Node and stack-allocated buffers for Go.

2025-02-27 — Design review notes from Rachel (Security): require metadata tamper-evidence for cross-account queue headers. Proposed HMAC header; security to review compliance implications for on-prem customers.
2025-03-01 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/412 — initial adapter implementation and unit tests for http and ws integrations. Needs perf tests and API polish.

2025-03-02 — Load testing (staging): simulated queue-fanout scenario with 5000 RPS. Observed sampling mismatch rate ~3% when worker coldstarts occur. Root cause: worker bootstrap clears sampler until rehydration completes. Action: add short-lived sampler token in rehydration header.

2025-03-04 — Next steps: add cross-language spec doc (JSON header schema), implement HMAC signing option, add automated e2e test harness (queue+worker+websocket), and schedule canary on internal traffic on 2025-03-14.
Developer notes: keep default behaviour conservative (no baggage autosync), expose explicit merge policy APIs (merge_replace, merge_append, merge_discard).
